extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense, focusing on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by prompting annotators with how-to instructions from instructables.com to generate goal-solution pairs and semantic perturbations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to articulate a physical goal based on an instructable, provide a valid solution, and provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Examples with low agreement during validation were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset underwent systematic data bias reduction using AFLite to discard instances with feature representations highly indicative of the target label.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of natural language understanding models.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA.

description.evidence: To study this question and begin bridging the representational gap, we introduce Physical Interaction: Question Answering , or PIQA to evaluate language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense. We focus on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.

creator.evidence: Yonatan Bisk1;2;3;4 Rowan Zellers1;4 Ronan Le Bras1 Jianfeng Gao2 Yejin Choi1;4

inLanguage.evidence: all data was collected in English.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect data with how-to instructions as a scaffold, and use state-of-the-art approaches for handling spurious biases, which we will discuss below.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Specifically, annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Our dataset is inspired by instructables.com, which provides users with instructions on how to build, craft, bake, or manipulate objects using everyday materials.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The dataset is further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm introduced in (Sakaguchi et al. 2020; Sap et al. 2019) which is an improvement on adversarial filtering

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: They would then articulate the goal (often centered on atypical materials) and how to achieve it. In addition, we asked them to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid, often subtly

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The AFLite algorithm performs a systematic data bias reduction: it discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In total our dataset is comprised of over 16,000 training QA pairs with an additional ~2K and ~3k held out for development and testing, respectively.
